chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: Chick Webb asks McRae to join on the road
summary: Back in New York, Bardu Ali relays Chick's request; McRae leaves the next morning with thirty-six dollars borrowed from Chick's band to travel.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And we were on our way in and we came in then. I was in town about two weeks and I was playing at the one of the bars at 141st and 7th Avenue, and Bardu Ali came on.
That was the guy, the leader -- directing Chick's band. "Hey, man, Chick told me you was back in town. Chick wanna see you.
I say, "Wanna see me?" He say, "Elmer Williams don't want to leave to go on the road." This is that hard year, '36 -- the summer of '36 -- April.
He says, "Come on over. Chick's down at the Brickwood," cross the street from a famous little club downstairs.

So, I went over and talked to him. He say, "Hey, I want you to join the band. Elmer don't want to leave. You want to go back on the road?"
I say, "Well, I'll have to talk with my wife about it, Chick, you know." He say, "Oh, tell her it ain't going to be for long, you know."

"I know."
Tell her
"You know it ain't going to be for on the road long. We're going to (inaudible) for a month or so." I say, "Okay."
I told my wife that Chick wanted me to go on the road. (Inaudible) talked to Chick. He say, "Hey, got any money?" I say, "Yeah, I got some money."
"I just came off the road with Lil Armstrong, man. (Inaudible) Charlie (inaudible)."
"Give me thirty-six dollars." This for joining (inaudible) Chick's band. Thirty-six dollars!
He say, "Meet me tomorrow morning at 8 o'clock. We leave here tomorrow morning."
